claims.statement: Prioritize unlocking G’hom Sek’kus early when Sardakk can reach five non-home planets without stretching its position.
claims.conditions: Nearby planets must be accessible without overcommitting ships; the unlock requires five planets outside the home system.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Podcast strategy, not current-rules verification.

claims.statement: Use adjacent-system commitment to attack planets without sending ships into the target system, while respecting its timing and route restrictions.
claims.conditions: Requires the commander, eligible ground forces in the active or adjacent systems, and a tactical action that reaches the commit step; do not assume tokened systems or prohibited routes qualify.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The FAQ clarifications were not all in the LRR at the time of recording.

claims.statement: Project the possibility of a ground invasion to negotiate access, objective cooperation, or peace before starting an expensive fight.
claims.conditions: Most useful with connected planets, an unlocked or imminent commander, and neighbors open to deals; intimidation is table-dependent.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts correct ‘fleet’ to ‘force’—often only a carrier plus nearby ground forces.

claims.statement: Use T’ro to add two infantry to a controlled planet in the active system after a tactical action, especially to reinforce a forward invasion lane.
claims.conditions: Once per round, after a tactical action, on a planet Sardakk controls in the active system.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The transcript briefly calls this a ‘Soul’ ability before describing the effect; this summary follows the described Sardakk agent text.

claims.statement: Use Sh’val’s hero for a high-value ground strike only when ships can reach the system and a likely win justifies returning them to reinforcements.
claims.conditions: Needs the unlocked hero, ships in the active system, enough ground forces to win, and a target worth the ships’ loss.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Target defenses and the ability to reach the system still matter.

claims.statement: Treat Light/Wave Deflectors as the key reach enabler for using Sh’val against a chosen target.
claims.conditions: Most valuable in a tech-rich game or when a decisive hero strike is plausible; the ordinary path expects it around round five.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Round-five Technology is not guaranteed, so this is a timing risk, not an assured combination.

claims.statement: Account for the mech’s sustain trigger and direct counters before committing Sardakk mechs.
claims.conditions: Strongest when mechs survive long enough to sustain in ground combat; check the target’s abilities and pre-combat losses.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Some surrounding ASR words are poor, but the trigger and Mentak exception are clear.

claims.statement: Count Unrelenting only on combat rolls; do not add it to space cannon, anti-fighter barrage, or bombardment ability rolls.
claims.conditions: Applies when estimating space or ground combat dice; keep separate ability rolls distinct.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Their ‘cowboy math’ is approximate, and action cards or table effects can change outcomes.

claims.statement: Do not plan around Exotrireme I bombardment or a dreadnought-heavy identity; the guide sees Sardakk mainly as a carrier-and-ground-force faction.
claims.conditions: Early capacity and broad planet reach usually matter more than bombardment; a board that rewards bombardment can change this.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: This is a strategic preference, not a claim that dreadnoughts are never useful.

claims.statement: Treat combat as a means to secure a point, planet, defense, or bargaining position—not as a scoring plan by itself.
claims.conditions: Before a fight, name the objective or position it advances; avoid fighting only because the dice are better.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Comparative faction rankings are podcast opinion, not universal results.

claims.statement: Plan around zero starting technologies and a weak economy instead of assuming Sardakk can keep pace without early research.
claims.conditions: Especially relevant with technology objectives, prerequisites, or a desired unit upgrade.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts explicitly exclude techless Sardakk from this guide; this is their competitive preference, not a universal requirement.

claims.statement: Expect planet-control objectives to be the more accessible category; do not confuse combat strength with broad scoring strength.
claims.conditions: Draft and expand toward the revealed objectives; technology and non-planet control asks can be unusually difficult.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: This assessment is broad and does not analyze a specific objective deck, map, or player count.

claims.statement: In a Milty-style draft, seek a planet-rich slice and connected planets or a ‘land bridge,’ especially if premium strategy cards are unlikely.
claims.conditions: Slice geometry matters more than assuming a favorable card pick; avoid a planetless gap along the intended route.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: This is anecdotal draft advice, not a guaranteed pattern.

claims.statement: Consider Warfare the preferred round-one primary pick when commander access and expansion leverage matter.
claims.conditions: Compare Warfare with Technology and Trade according to slice and economy.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts reject ‘always’ preferences and make card selection conditional on the actual game.

claims.statement: Follow Technology in round one even if another card is the primary pick; double technology only when its immediate value justifies a round-one build sacrifice.
claims.conditions: Double tech suits a position with favorable costs and enough time to recover the fleet; selecting Warfare does not replace following Technology.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Techless variants exist, but the guide excludes them; ‘must’ reflects its preferred plan.

claims.statement: Take Trade as a round-one alternative when cash is needed to build units and still afford a Technology follow.
claims.conditions: Favor Trade when cash or commodity exchange is binding; favor Warfare when expansion and threat projection dominate.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Trade helps the opening but does not remove Sardakk’s structural economy problem.

claims.statement: Prioritize Dark Energy Tap (DET) as an early exploration investment when the slice offers safe access.
claims.conditions: Budget the command tokens for exploration; avoid routes made dangerous by anomalies or enemy space cannon.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: One nearby retreat sentence is transcribed as “BET,” likely DET from context; individual exploration draws remain uncertain.

claims.statement: Treat Gravity Drive and Carrier II as the core movement-and-capacity package, not a complete winning plan by themselves.
claims.conditions: Prioritize in blue-focused paths; skips and bonus research can alter order.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers do not prescribe one fixed sequence for every slice.

claims.statement: Use Sling Relay to ease production limits, especially when it can add a capital ship alongside normal fighter and infantry builds.
claims.conditions: Useful when research tempo permits and production is binding; an alternative Exotrireme path gives it up.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The unit mix is an example, not a universal recipe.

claims.statement: Treat Fighter II and Bio-Stims from a green skip as optional additions after the core blue path and Light/Wave.
claims.conditions: Requires bonus tech tempo; protect resources and tokens needed for scoring and production.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: A stall action is not a pass, and the hosts’ hit-threshold math is approximate.

claims.statement: Pursue Exotrireme II on the flashy late-game path only when both yellow and blue skips make room without sacrificing Light/Wave.
claims.conditions: Needs both skips and enough research tempo; the default route already expects Light/Wave near round five.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: This is a possible high-upside line, not a routine plan.

claims.statement: Usually avoid a red-skip detour and Valkyrie Particle Weave; the guide calls it costly win-more research, not a needed ground-combat fix.
claims.conditions: Reconsider only when concrete objectives, discounts, or bonus research make it timely.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Low research frequency is anecdotal in the episode, not measured evidence.

claims.statement: Remember Exotrireme II’s ship-destruction ability when attacking Sardakk, but first check that the upgrade is actually present.
claims.conditions: Attackers should plan capacity for possible ship losses; the ability matters only if the unit survives to use it.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: This reports the episode’s explanation, not an independent current-rules ruling.

claims.statement: Advertise and sell Tekklar Legion near the ground-combat window; accept a modest offer rather than expecting it to sell itself.
claims.conditions: Best when the buyer expects a consequential ground fight and can use the note at the relevant timing window.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Market value depends on table behavior; current mechanics are not reviewed.

claims.statement: Arrange an Alliance buyer early and favor a partner that can keep ground forces positioned for adjacent-system commitments.
claims.conditions: Buyer, terrain, and unit mix determine value; Sardakk itself is particularly built to exploit the commander.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 379 Super Guide, published 2024-11-27; current ruleset compatibility not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: This is a tentative market assessment from the hosts.

connections.conditions: T’ro puts infantry on an active front that can support adjacent-system commitment.
Both can threaten ground invasions without relying on winning ordinary space combat; the hero is a more costly, decisive strike.
Light/Wave improves the chance Sardakk ships can reach the hero’s chosen active system.
Sling Relay supplements home production; T’ro adds infantry at the active front.
Particle Weave can add a ground-combat hit alongside the mech’s sustain-triggered hit; the guide considers the tech too costly as a default.
The guide treats both as the core blue movement-and-capacity package; order may vary with skips.
If Exotrireme II survives a combat round, the described ability can remove up to two ships and threaten carrier capacity.
The guide likes Fighter II because improved fighters also receive Sardakk’s combat-roll modifier; hit-threshold math is approximate.
